title: Expose executable realtime profile through installed API
requires: Installed public SDK test toolchain and at least the Slang CPU production driver
scope: Replace the F8-23 rejected native profile stub with truthful execution-profile enumeration and selection after production scheduling exists. Add installed-public-API observation generation; do not claim physical qualification or change advertised interaction capabilities.
acceptance: Eligible production adapters enumerate realtime-single-step 1.0 and accept its immutable simulation-create request; missing extension, unknown name, incompatible version, invalid chain, timestep outside one binary32 ULP and substeps other than one fail without fallback.

An installed C consumer performs the frozen public sequence through submission, fence wait, simulation status, statistics and copied public state with validation both disabled and enabled on the Slang CPU driver.

The public observation record identifies installed API use, exact profile/candidate inputs and complete step/work counters required by realtime_oracle.py; private state and mock-driver execution cannot satisfy native evidence.
Loader, validation, ABI, installed-SDK and legacy omission regressions pass; unsupported domains and adapters remain explicit rather than inheriting profile support.

history.reason: Production adapters expose the immutable realtime profile; relocated installed C consumers produce oracle-validated public observations with validation off and on.
